Where it began

Kevin Pietersen was born in Pietermaritzburg, in what was then Natal Province, on 27 June 1980, to an English mother and an Afrikaner father. He grew up one of four brothers and went to Maritzburg College. As a boy he played hockey, tennis and squash too, which he felt gave him a strong right arm for batting.

He began in first-class cricket for Natal in 1997, aged 17, mostly as an off-spinner who could hit a ball hard down the order. In 2000 he spent a summer with Cannock in the Midlands, living in a single room at the club. Clive Rice, the Nottinghamshire coach, had seen him at a schools festival and offered him a county contract. Pietersen said yes at once, and after four years in county cricket he was eligible to play for England.

The player

His Test debut came at Lord's in the 2005 Ashes, and he made a fifty in each innings. At The Oval, with the series on the line, he made 158, hitting seven sixes, and England had the Ashes back. He went on to play 104 Tests up to 2014, scoring 8,181 runs at 47.29 with 23 hundreds and a best of 227. He also took ten wickets with his off-spin and held 62 catches.

In the shorter game he was just as dangerous. He was named player of the series when England won the 2010 World Twenty20, the country's first global title, and in 2007 he was ranked the best one-day batter in the world.

What made him special

Pietersen batted as if bowlers were there to be taken on. He scored quickly in every format and reached 1,000, then 2,000, one-day runs as quickly as anyone ever had. Against Muttiah Muralitharan he swept for six from the wrong side, and later he took to switching his hands and stance as the bowler ran in, turning himself into a left-hander for one ball. Some wanted the shot outlawed; the rest of us wanted to see it again.

The flip side of all that adventure was that every so often he got out playing the shot of the day. Most of the time, though, the shot of the day was his.

Away from the middle

He played franchise cricket around the world, in the IPL, the Big Bash, the Caribbean and Pakistan, and later became mentor of Delhi Capitals for the 2025 IPL. He gave his earnings from a 2017 season with Surrey to rhino conservation. He was made an MBE and named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year, and in 2018 he was picked in England's greatest Test XI.

In 2007 he married the singer Jessica Taylor, with his old team-mate Darren Gough as best man.

And finally

At the 2005 Ashes he batted with a dyed blond stripe down the middle of his head. It was not to everyone's taste, but nobody remembered the hair for long. They remembered the sixes.
